requirements.statement: One scaffold-project.sh --rebase call copies every framework component into the target's .claude/, adding absent files, replacing files whose bytes differ, and leaving byte-identical files alone.
requirements.source: investigation Objectives O1; TRD §Objectives O1 (must pass: yes)

requirements.statement: The same call removes retired framework files named in one declared retired list (a data file); files neither on that list nor shipped by the plugin are preserved. A test keeps the list in step with the retired tables in rebase-project.md and with the plugin.
requirements.source: investigation Objectives O2; TRD §Objectives O2 (must pass: yes)

requirements.statement: Library-skill selection uses the selection file and reconcile_selected_skills(); the engine reads no stack.md table and does no capability-word inference.
requirements.source: investigation Objectives O3; TRD §Objectives O3 (must pass: not marked)

requirements.statement: The engine merges .claude/settings.json: ensemble-owned hooks block regenerated from the plugin default; non-ensemble registrations carried forward per event (compared as whole registrations, never de-duplicated by filename); registrations pointing at retired hooks dropped; other local keys kept.
requirements.source: investigation Objectives O4; TRD §Objectives O4 (must pass: yes)

requirements.statement: The engine refuses to write settings.json when the merged hooks block has fewer registrations, or fewer prompt-type entries, than the plugin default, and reports the refusal.
requirements.source: investigation Objectives O5; TRD §Objectives O5 (must pass: yes)

requirements.statement: After copying, the engine sets the execute bit on every manifest hook, re-injects agent skill preloads, stamps the version through the strict stamp, and runs the existing git-files and records-cutover steps.
requirements.source: investigation Objectives O6; TRD §Objectives O6 (must pass: not marked)

requirements.statement: A vendored framework file the owner has edited is reported as a conflict and left byte-identical. Owner edit vs older shipped version is decided by hash: a hash matching a version the framework shipped in a release is replaced; one matching none is a conflict.
requirements.source: investigation Objectives O7; TRD §Objectives O7 (must pass: yes)

requirements.statement: A settings.json key the engine cannot merge is reported as a conflict and its local value left as it was. If the unmergeable part is the hooks block, or the file is not JSON, the merge writes nothing to the file. The strict stamp (O6) still writes its own fields unless the file is not JSON.
requirements.source: investigation Objectives O8; TRD §Objectives O8 (clarified; must pass: not marked)

requirements.statement: The engine prints one machine-readable result: per category (commands, agents, hooks, hook-libs, hook-prompts, workflows, libs, contracts, skills, rules, settings), lists added, replaced, removed, unchanged, preserved, conflicts.
requirements.source: investigation Objectives O9; TRD §Objectives O9 (must pass: yes)

requirements.statement: Under a dry-run flag the engine computes and prints the same result and writes nothing: the target's file tree, file modes and git index are unchanged.
requirements.source: investigation Objectives O10; TRD §Objectives O10 (must pass: yes)

requirements.statement: Under --preserve-all the engine follows the documented meaning of that flag, except that the ensemble-owned hooks block in settings.json is still regenerated and ensemble-owned registrations still dropped (the departure is recorded as D14, an OWNER-CALL).
requirements.source: roadmap item 2; TRD §Objectives O11 (corrected and clarified against rebase-project.md; must pass: not marked)

requirements.statement: The engine never writes constitution.md, stack.md, process.md, verification.md, design.md or ship.md, in any mode.
requirements.source: investigation Objectives O12; TRD §Objectives O12 (must pass: yes)

requirements.statement: --refresh keeps its present contract: never creates a component directory, never deletes a file; its existing tests stay green.
requirements.source: investigation Objectives O13; TRD §Objectives O13 (must pass: yes)

requirements.statement: Running the engine a second time on its own output reports empty added, replaced and removed lists in every category, and changes no file's bytes or mode except the refreshed_at and rebased_at timestamp fields the strict stamp writes.
requirements.source: roadmap item 2 'How it will be checked'; TRD §Objectives O14 (corrected; must pass: yes)

requirements.statement: New BATS cases prove O1, O2, O4, O5, O7, O8, O10, O12, O13 and O14, and the full battery (npx jest, BATS suites, pytest) shows no test that passed on the pre-change code now failing and no suite passing fewer tests, measured against a same-install baseline (D18).
requirements.source: investigation Objectives O15; TRD §Objectives O15 (clarified; must pass: not marked)

requirements.statement: Every path the engine writes or deletes resolves inside the target's .claude/ directory, whatever a data file or a symlink in the target says.

Unit coverage at least 60% (constitution Quality Gates), measured for retired-files.test.js by npx jest --coverage and for rebase_engine_program() by python3 -m trace in RBE-T001; reported as met or not met.
requirements.source: TRD §6.1 Testing Requirements (not an objective row; a measurable quality promise)

requirements.statement: Integration coverage at least 50% when applicable; RBE-T001 aged-fixture case drives the whole --rebase mode. Not measured and not claimed met (stated gap).
Documentation updated: CHANGELOG.md entry for the --rebase mode, its data files, the generator and the release step, with a Not-yet-proven list.
requirements.source: constitution.md Quality Gates ('Documentation updated'); TRD task RBE-D001

In scaffold-project.sh: parse --rebase, --dry-run, --preserve-all with exclusivity rules; resolve --plugin-dir to absolute; add authored_rules(); add render_plugin_tree() (D4, D13); add normhash mode to agent_skills_program() and exclude list to inject (D7, D17). Stub --rebase dispatch until RBE-B002. Serves D1, D4, D7, D13, D15. Deps: none.

Write packages/core/scripts/generate-shipped-hashes.sh (--seed, --append <tag>, --check; D8); run --seed and commit packages/core/templates/shipped-hashes.json; add coverage-check paths to retired-files.json; commit older-version fixtures in test/fixtures/rebase-engine/. Add settings merge (D11), its conflicts and the guard mode wired before the one settings write (D12), and preserve-all's settings rule (D14) to the planner and applier. Serves O4, O5, O8, O11. Deps: RBE-B002.

Wire post-copy steps in D17 order (hook modes, reconcile_selected_skills, inject_agent_skills excluding conflicted agents, git files, records cutover, stamp_ensemble_version strict last) and report each in steps. Serves O3, O6, O7, O14. Deps: RBE-B003.

One aged-fixture BATS case across the whole engine (older shipped file, missing file, retired file, user agent, user hook registration, owner-edited framework file, owner-filled verification.md): apply, dry-run on a copy, second apply; plus --refresh on a tree with a retired file. Then full battery against pre-change baseline (D18) and measure coverage per §6.1. Serves O13, O14, O15, D18, constitution Quality Gates (coverage). Deps: RBE-B004.

Add CHANGELOG.md entry for the --rebase mode, its two data files, the generator and the release step (generate-shipped-hashes.sh --append <previous tag>), with a Not-yet-proven list. Serves constitution Quality Gates (Documentation updated), D8, OQ-9. Deps: RBE-B004.

open_questions: TRD OQ-1 | Is autonomy.md owner-governed? (roadmap open question 1; owner-only) | Assumed: No: it stays framework-shipped and is replaced when it is an older shipped version; an owner-edited copy is a conflict and left untouched (the owner's recorded default). Why it matters: Decides whether one more file joins AUTHORED_RULES. If wrong: Add it to the one line in authored_rules() (D15) and to owner-rules.js, which a test keeps equal.

TRD OQ-2 | Should --refresh also remove retired files? (roadmap open question 3; owner-only) | Assumed: No: only --rebase removes. Why it matters: O13. If wrong: A separate change to the refresh contract.

TRD OQ-3 | How an owner edit is told apart from an older shipped file | Assumed: D6 and D8: one plugin list of the hashes every v* release installed, built by rendering each tag with its own scaffold; the current plugin's bytes by direct comparison; no per-project record (OWNER-CALL, recorded by Forge in the 1.1.0 review). Why it matters: O7. If wrong: Swap the mechanism inside the planner and generator; the result format is unchanged.

TRD OQ-4 | The investigation's O11 said preserve-all replaces and removes nothing; rebase-project.md documents that it still replaces commands, hooks, workflows, libs and contracts | Assumed: Followed the documented table (the roadmap fences off changing the flag's meaning); preserve-all removes nothing in any category, and still regenerates the hooks block (D14, OWNER-CALL). Why it matters: Preserve-all output differs between the two readings. If wrong: Change D14's category table; one BATS case changes.

TRD OQ-5 | A second run reports zero changes vs the strict stamp writing refreshed_at/rebased_at every run | Assumed: O14 allows those two fields to change; the stamp still runs on every apply, last, as rebase-project.md line 1166 documents. Why it matters: Strict byte-identity would require skipping the stamp on an empty plan. If wrong: Skip the stamp when the plan is empty and the version is unchanged; RBE-B004's criterion tightens.

TRD OQ-6 | D8 asks each release to append the previous tag, and the history check fails on a full clone until it does | Assumed: Accepted: once per release, the failing check names the command, and CI is unaffected (TR4). Why it matters: A forgotten append makes the files of the newest release before the current one read as owner edits. If wrong: Move the append into the release PR checklist, or drop the history part of --check.

TRD OQ-7 | Today's prose may add a library skill matching the stack; the engine never adds an uninstalled library skill | Assumed: Accepted, as the owner ruled out the stack table; /init-project still selects. Why it matters: A project whose stack gained a language gets no new skill from a rebase. If wrong: Add an explicit add-skill path that reads selected-skills.txt lines with no folder.

TRD OQ-8 | An owner-edited retired file is deleted like an unedited one | Assumed: Accepted (NG9): the list is a declared deletion list, and git is the undo. Why it matters: An owner's annotation on a retired file is lost from the tree (recoverable from git). If wrong: Classify retired files by D6 too and report edited ones as conflicts.

TRD OQ-9 | --refresh (run at SessionStart after every plugin upgrade) already replaces framework files without comparing bytes, so O7 protects only edits made since the last upgrade, or with refresh turned off. Should refresh skip owner-edited files using the same hash list? (owner-only) | Assumed: No change to refresh in this feature (out-of-scope fence; NG4, O13). Why it matters: With refresh on, most owner edits are already gone by the time a rebase runs, so O7 rarely has one to protect. If wrong: A separate change to refresh_project() that consults shipped-hashes.json before each replace.

TRD OQ-10 | Should the 15 unprefixed release tags (4.1.9 to 4.1.23) be rendered too? | Assumed: No: D8 renders v* tags, per the review; installs from 4.1.x read their differing files as conflicts (fail safe). Why it matters: Projects still on a 4.1.x install get conflicts instead of replacements. If wrong: generate-shipped-hashes.sh --append 4.1.23 (and earlier) adds them; the tag check compares v* tags only.

Investigation OQ-1 | Is autonomy.md owner-governed? (owner-only) | Assumed: It stays framework-shipped and is replaced when it is an older shipped version; an owner-edited copy is a conflict and left untouched.
Investigation OQ-2 | Should --refresh also remove retired files? (owner-only) | Assumed: No: only --rebase removes; --refresh keeps never-create/never-delete.

Investigation OQ-3 | How an owner edit is told apart from an older shipped file | Assumed: One shipped-hash list in the plugin, built by rendering every v* release tag with that tag's own scaffold; the current plugin's bytes recognised by direct comparison; no per-project record. Installs from untagged builds read as conflicts, the fail-safe direction.

Investigation OQ-9 | --refresh already replaces framework files without comparing bytes, so O7's conflict detection protects only edits made since the last upgrade, or with refresh turned off. Should refresh skip owner-edited files using the same hash list? (owner-only) | Assumed: No change to refresh in this feature (out-of-scope fence; O13).
could_not_verify: Claim: normalise(strip(...)) removes the preload block every v* tag's scaffold wrote, not just today's (13 of 13 current agents measured 2026-10-12 by the sibling TRD) | How I'd check it: After --seed, render each tag twice with different skill selections and compare the two normhash outputs per agent (RBE-P002 proves one tag through its fixture) | Why not checked: Needs normhash (RBE-B001) and 48 tag renders; neither exists yet.

Claim: Every v* tag's own scaffold renders cleanly outside a git work tree with an absolute --plugin-dir and --copy-skills (four tags' scripts read for the flags, none run) | How I'd check it: Run --seed (RBE-P002); it stops on the first tag that fails | Why not checked: Needs the generator (RBE-P002); a document audit runs no tag.

Claim: What a tag's render installs equals what a real install of that tag received | How I'd check it: Compare a render of v4.15.0 with a project scaffolded from a v4.15.0 marketplace install | Why not checked: Needs a marketplace install of an old tag, outside the audit's read-only scope.

Claim: How many projects hold files from an untagged build (TR1) | How I'd check it: Count conflicts across the first real --rebase runs in F-3 | Why not checked: Only observable once F-3 calls the engine on real projects.

Claim: How many owner edits survive --refresh to reach a rebase at all (OQ-9) | How I'd check it: Check projects with refresh on for vendored files that differ from every listed hash | Why not checked: Needs real projects and the committed shipped-hashes.json.

Claim: A cp -RL packages/full copy behaves like a marketplace cache install for the render | How I'd check it: Render from both and compare their file lists | Why not checked: Needs a render (RBE-B001) and a real cache install.

Claim: The constitution's 60% unit floor is met by the bash in --rebase, render_plugin_tree and generate-shipped-hashes.sh | How I'd check it: Install a bash coverage tool (kcov or bashcov; neither installed nor listed in stack.md) and run the BATS cases under it | Why not checked: No bash coverage tool exists here; TRD §6.1 records it as a stated gap rather than a met floor.

Claim: The constitution's 50% integration floor is met by RBE-T001's whole-mode case | How I'd check it: As above: the integration path is bash driving the Python program as a subprocess | Why not checked: Same missing bash coverage tool; stated gap in TRD §6.1.

Investigation file has no Could Not Verify section; it was checked and none exists. TRD Could Not Verify rows are the 8 above (6 claims plus the two coverage-floor rows). No PRD exists for this feature: the TRD header names the investigation as its source PRD.
